subject: Concealing cables and equipment
hook: Where do the cables go on a media wall with nothing on show? Watch the route get built in.
ig:
Where do the cables go on a media wall with nothing on show? Watch the route get built in.

A clean media wall is not about hiding wires with clips and covers. The route is designed into the unit from the start:

• A void is left behind the back panel, so cables run vertically from the TV down to the equipment area.
• Cable holes are placed where each device actually sits, not in a guessed position.
• A removable access panel means you can add a console or swap a router later without taking the unit apart.
• On fitting day, cables are fed through before the TV is mounted, so nothing has to be squeezed in afterwards.

The result is a wall that looks simple, because all the thinking is behind it.

Planning a media wall? Comment CABLES and we will send you the link to our media walls page.
fb:
We often get asked how a media wall ends up with no cables showing at all. This is how.

The route is built into the unit in our Hanley workshop: a void behind the back panel, cable holes placed exactly where the equipment sits, and a panel that lifts out so you can get to everything later. On fitting day, the cables go through before the TV goes up.

No trunking, no clips, no tangle behind the soundbar. If you are thinking about a media wall for the living room, take a look at what we build here:
